prompt.context_jp: 事務所の空気___、いつになく張りつめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事務所の空気___、いつになく張りつめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the office atmosphere as the established topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is describing a known setting (the office) and commenting on its state. は frames 空気 as the topic about which a comment is made.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the atmosphere as brand-new information, which clashes with this scene-setting narration about an already-established office.

contrast_examples.jp: 空気は張りつめていた。

prompt.context_jp: 「西尾院長とも 黒いつながり___ ありそうですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 西尾院長とも 黒いつながり___ ありそうですね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the existence of shady ties as new information.

feedback.correct_en: ある/ありそう with a newly-introduced noun takes が — Nana is pointing out the existence of connections as a fresh observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose 黒いつながり as an established topic, but here it's newly surfaced.

contrast_examples.en: As for the connection, there is one (contrastive).

prompt.context_jp: 振り返った先には、記者証を提げた見知らぬ男___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 振り返った先には、記者証を提げた見知らぬ男___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the appearance of an unknown figure in the scene.

feedback.correct_en: 見知らぬ男 is brand-new information suddenly discovered when Nana turns around. New-entity existence/appearance takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the man was already an established topic, which contradicts 見知らぬ (unfamiliar).

prompt.context_jp: 「ドラマにしかいませんよ そんな男」→ 「そんな男___ドラマにしかいませんよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: そんな男___ドラマにしかいませんよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the fronted topic 'that kind of man'.

feedback.correct_en: そんな男 is fronted as the topic being evaluated/commented on: 'As for that kind of man, he only exists in dramas.' は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark new information presentation, not a general evaluative comment on a type of man.

contrast_examples.en: That kind of man doesn't exist (topic-comment).

prompt.context_jp: 革張りの椅子に沈み込んだ西尾忠彦___、あからさまに苛立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 西尾忠彦___、あからさまに苛立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the established character being described.

feedback.correct_en: Nishio is the scene's topic; the narrator comments on his mood. は marks him as the topic of discussion.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Nishio as newly introduced info, but he is already established and being described.

prompt.context_jp: それが息子の粗相で早々に呼び戻され、機嫌___目に見えて悪かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 機嫌___目に見えて悪かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the body/mood state being described of an established subject.

feedback.correct_en: 機嫌 belongs to the already-established Nishio; the narrator comments on his mood as a topic. は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal fresh presentation, but we're continuing the description of Nishio's state.

prompt.context_jp: 扉___乱暴に開かれたのは、その平穏を打ち破るような勢いだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 扉___乱暴に開かれたのは、その平穏を打ち破るような勢いだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside this nominalized relative clause marking the door's action.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative/nominalized clause (…のは), the subject takes が. 扉 is the subject of 開かれた within the clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は cannot normally appear as the subject marker inside a relative clause — it marks a sentence-level topic.

contrast_examples.en: The moment the door opened (relative clause).

prompt.context_jp: 「潔癖な日本人___ ウソ___嫌いなんですよ」(first blank)
prompt.prompt_jp: 潔癖な日本人___ ウソが嫌いなんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'clean-minded Japanese' as the generic topic.

feedback.correct_en: Generic statements about a group use は to set the topic: 'As for clean-minded Japanese, they hate lies.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify the Japanese as the unique haters of lies, which is not the generic claim being made.

contrast_examples.jp: 日本人はウソが嫌いだ。
日本人がウソが嫌いだ。
contrast_examples.en: It's the Japanese who hate lies (exhaustive, odd here).

prompt.context_jp: 潔癖な日本人はウソ___嫌いなんですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 潔癖な日本人はウソ___嫌いなんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the object of the emotion 嫌い.

feedback.correct_en: Stative emotion adjectives like 好き/嫌い mark their object with が, not を.
feedback.incorrect_en: を marks objects of transitive verbs. 嫌い is a na-adjective, not a verb, so を is ungrammatical.

prompt.context_jp: 翌日の会見場___、フラッシュの光で満たされていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 翌日の会見場___、フラッシュの光で満たされていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the scene's topic location.

feedback.correct_en: The narrative sets the conference venue as the topic and describes what filled it. は functions as scene-setting topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the venue as surprising new info, but the sentence simply describes its state.

contrast_examples.jp: 会見場はフラッシュで満たされていた。
contrast_examples.en: The venue was filled with flashes (topic-comment).

contrast_examples.jp: 会見場がフラッシュで満ちた。
contrast_examples.en: The venue (of all places) got filled (event focus).

prompt.context_jp: 粟田口大臣の計らいで 厚労省___ ポストを用意してもらえる
prompt.prompt_jp: 厚労省___ ポストを用意してもらえる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the Ministry as the destination/location where a post will be set up for him.

feedback.correct_en: ポストを用意する takes に to mark the organization where the position will exist — 'a post AT the Ministry'.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the Ministry as the location of an action event, but here we're specifying where the post will reside.

contrast_examples.jp: 大学にポストを用意する。
contrast_examples.en: Prepare a post at the university.
Hold a meeting at the university.

prompt.context_jp: 数年後には この病院___ お前のものだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 数年後には この病院___ お前のものだ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'this hospital' as the topic being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: The father is predicating about a known referent (this hospital). は fits an A は B だ equational topic-comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would give exhaustive focus 'it is THIS hospital (not another) that will be yours', which doesn't match the context.

contrast_examples.jp: この病院はお前のものだ。
この病院がお前のものだ。
contrast_examples.en: THIS hospital is the one that's yours (exhaustive).

prompt.context_jp: 「追放になるのは 三好先生___ありませんが」
prompt.prompt_jp: 追放になるのは 三好先生___ありませんが
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that carries a contrastive 'not Miyoshi (but someone else)' nuance.

feedback.correct_en: The は in ではありません delivers contrastive negation: 'It won't be Miyoshi (it'll be someone else).' The speaker implies a contrasting alternative.
feedback.incorrect_en: 三好先生がありません is ungrammatical here — this is a copular identification, not an existence claim.

contrast_examples.en: The culprit isn't him (implying it's someone else).

contrast_examples.jp: 追放されるのは私ではない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not me who'll be expelled.

prompt.context_jp: 先生は 慶西大を卒業___していますが 入学___していないようですね
prompt.prompt_jp: 卒業___していますが 入学___していないようですね (same particle both blanks)
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that creates the contrast 'graduated BUT didn't enroll'.

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は attached after を/に (卒業は/入学は) sets up a sharp 'X yes, but Y no' contrast between two parallel actions.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using が would simply mark the object without the pointed contrast; the biting rhetorical effect comes from は.

contrast_examples.jp: 食べはしたが、好きではない。
contrast_examples.en: I did eat it, but I don't like it.

contrast_examples.jp: 行きはしないが、見はする。
contrast_examples.en: I won't go, but I will watch.

prompt.context_jp: 「数字___？ 裏金の金額よ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 数字___？ 裏金の金額よ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the numbers' as the topic being asked about.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for the numbers?' — questioning what one specific item means in a list of items. は picks out each item as a topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: 数字が？ would sound like 'The numbers?! (as subject of what?)' — incomplete and unnatural here.

prompt.context_jp: 「バカって言うヤツのほう___ バカなんだよ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: バカって言うヤツのほう___ バカなんだよ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that exhaustively identifies 'the one who calls others idiot' as THE idiot.

feedback.correct_en: 〜のほうが is a fixed comparative/identificational structure: 'It's the one who calls others stupid who's actually the stupid one.' が signals exhaustive identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: ほうは would lose the sharp 'THAT one, not you' pointing. The whole retort hinges on exhaustive が.

contrast_examples.en: HE'S the one at fault (not me).

prompt.context_jp: 殴りつけた瞬間の記憶___、まだ拳の芯にひどく痛い熱として残っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 殴りつけた瞬間の記憶___、まだ拳の芯に…残っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the memory as the sentence topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: The opening sentence takes 'the memory' as its topic and comments on its continuing state. は is standard for such topic-setting openings.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the memory as surprising new info, but this is a reflective introspective narration.

contrast_examples.jp: 記憶はまだ残っている。

prompt.context_jp: ここは医大専門の予備校だな 慶西をはじめ 一流の医大に 多くの受験生を___
prompt.prompt_jp: 多くの受験生を___している
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'get many students to pass' in the exam context?

feedback.correct_en: The school makes/causes students to pass — causative 合格させる is the correct voice for a third party enabling passing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 合格して (plain) would mean the school itself passes. 合格されて (passive) sounds like being passed upon, which is nonsensical.

prompt.context_jp: 学会を口実に、しばらくは___を伸ばしておく算段だったらしい。
prompt.prompt_jp: しばらくは___を伸ばしておく算段
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom meaning 'to relax / let loose'?

feedback.correct_en: 羽を伸ばす literally 'stretch one's wings' is the set idiom for cutting loose away from constraints.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を伸ばす means 'reach out'; 足を伸ばす means 'extend one's trip/legs' — neither captures the 'let loose' nuance.

contrast_examples.en: Let loose at the business trip destination.
Extend the trip to the hot spring.

prompt.context_jp: 「記者が___きたのか」
prompt.prompt_jp: 記者が___きたのか
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'sniffed out / caught wind of' a scandal?

feedback.correct_en: 嗅ぎつける is the idiomatic verb for reporters/investigators sniffing out hidden information.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見つける (simply find) and 気づく (notice) lack the connotation of actively tracking down a scent-trail.

contrast_examples.jp: 記者がスキャンダルを嗅ぎつけた。
contrast_examples.en: The reporter sniffed out a scandal.

prompt.context_jp: 辞めさせた女が___に マスコミにバラしたんじゃ ないんですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 辞めさせた女が___にマスコミにバラした
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'out of spite / in retaliation'?

feedback.correct_en: 腹いせに is the set adverbial 'out of spite/to vent resentment', fitting a fired woman leaking to the press.
feedback.incorrect_en: 嫌がらせ means 'harassment' (an act, not a motive adverb). 仕返しに is close but less idiomatic here; the original is 腹いせに.

prompt.context_jp: ___日本人は ウソが嫌いなんですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: ___日本人はウソが嫌いなんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which adjective means 'puritanical / fastidiously honest'?

feedback.correct_en: 潔癖 describes someone morally fastidious — intolerant of impurity or dishonesty. It fits the claim about Japanese attitudes to lying.
feedback.incorrect_en: 清潔 means physically clean; 純潔 means chaste/pure (often sexual). Neither captures moral intolerance of lies.

prompt.context_jp: 「___に 何だ？ 失礼だぞ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___に 何だ？ 失礼だぞ
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'out of the blue / without warning'?

feedback.correct_en: やぶから棒に = 'abruptly, out of the blue' — Nishio reacts to the lawyer's sudden intrusion.
feedback.incorrect_en: 寝耳に水 means 'bolt from the blue' as a noun phrase (surprise news), not an adverbial '〜に 何だ' intro. 棚からぼた餅 means unexpected good luck.

contrast_examples.jp: やぶから棒に質問する。

contrast_examples.en: News that comes as a complete shock.

prompt.context_jp: 余計な___かもしれませんが…お得意の裏口からお帰りください
prompt.prompt_jp: 余計な___かもしれませんが
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits the polite phrase '(I'm being) meddlesome, but...'?

feedback.correct_en: 余計なお世話 is the fixed phrase 'unwanted interference/none of my business', used ironically here by Chiyo.
feedback.incorrect_en: 余計な心配 (worry) exists but lacks the sarcastic 'meddling' punch. 余計な気持ち is not idiomatic.

prompt.context_jp: スキャンダルを ___とするウソほど バレたときはたたかれるんです
prompt.prompt_jp: スキャンダルを___とするウソ
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'try to conceal/cover up' a scandal?

feedback.correct_en: 隠す (transitive, 'hide/conceal') → volitional 隠そう, fitting '…を隠そうとするウソ' (a lie that tries to hide a scandal).
feedback.incorrect_en: 隠れる is intransitive 'be hidden/take cover' — wrong voice for an object. 隠され is passive stem, not a volitional.

prompt.context_jp: Chiyo deflating the ex-director: he claims power, she cuts him down.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as a cutting, deliberately polite put-down?

choices.text: 失礼ですが 誰でもないかと思います
失礼ですが あなたは誰でもないです

feedback.correct_en: 〜かと思います softens the statement into a devastatingly polite opinion — more cutting than direct assertion in Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: The direct 誰でもないです sounds blunt and un-secretarial; the irony depends on the hedged politeness.

contrast_examples.en: I believe that's not quite right (polite put-down).

prompt.context_jp: Sitting down at a mahjong table against an opponent.
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting is natural when starting a game/match?

choices.text: やさしくしてください

feedback.correct_en: お手柔らかに is the set phrase for 'go easy on me' at games/matches — concise and idiomatic.
feedback.incorrect_en: やさしくしてください is grammatically fine but sounds like a plea in a relationship, not a sportsman's remark.

contrast_examples.jp: 一局 お手柔らかに。
contrast_examples.en: Go easy on me this round.

prompt.context_jp: Sarang rejecting improper receipts.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the natural accounting idiom for 'cannot be claimed as business expenses'?

feedback.correct_en: 経費で落ちる/落とす is the fixed accounting idiom: '落ちる' = 'be writable as an expense'. Negative 落ちません = 'can't be expensed'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 下がる means 'go down/decrease' and doesn't form an accounting collocation here.

contrast_examples.jp: これは経費で落ちない。

prompt.context_jp: Reacting to Nishio's slick damage-control press conference.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as 'the damage-control was a total success'?

choices.text: 火を消すこと大成功か

feedback.correct_en: 火消し is the established noun meaning 'damage control / putting out a (PR) fire' — concise and idiomatic.
feedback.incorrect_en: 火を消すこと is a literal verbal nominalization about extinguishing physical fire — unnatural for a scandal context.

prompt.context_jp: Awataguchi lecturing Nishio about cover-ups.
prompt.prompt_en: Which variant sounds more natural for the proverb-like punchline?

choices.text: スキャンダルを隠そうとするウソほど バレたときはたたかれるんです
スキャンダルを隠したいウソほど バレるときはたたかれるんです

feedback.correct_en: 隠そうとする (actively try to hide) + バレたとき (when exposed) creates the idiomatic cause→consequence rhythm the line needs.
feedback.incorrect_en: 隠したい (want to hide) shifts focus to desire, not action, and バレるとき (nonpast) misses the condition 'once it IS exposed'.

contrast_examples.jp: 隠そうとするほどバレる。
contrast_examples.en: The more you try to hide, the more it leaks.

contrast_examples.jp: バレたときに追及される。
contrast_examples.en: You get grilled WHEN it comes out.
